Format: \"Source: [System/Document], [Date], [Specific Reference], [URL if applicable]\"\n    60\t- Examples:\n    61\t  - \"Source: Company 10-K, FY2024, Page 45, Revenue Note, [SEC EDGAR URL]\"\n    62\t  - \"Source: Company 10-Q, Q2 2025, Exhibit 99.1, [SEC EDGAR URL]\"\n    63\t  - \"Source: Bloomberg Terminal, 8/15/2025, AAPL US Equity\"\n    64\t  - \"Source: FactSet, 8/20/2025, Consensus Estimates Screen\"\n    65\t\n    66\t# XLSX creation, editing, and analysis\n    67\t\n    68\t## Overview\n    69\t\n    70\tA user may ask you to create, edit, or analyze the contents of an .xlsx file. You have different tools and workflows available for different tasks.\n    71\t\n    72\t## Important Requirements\n    73\t\n    74\t**LibreOffice Required for Formula Recalculation**: You can assume LibreOffice is installed for recalculating formula values using the `scripts/recalc.py` script. The script automatically configures LibreOffice on first run, including in sandboxed environments where Unix sockets are restricted (handled by `scripts/office/soffice.py`)\n    75\t\n    76\t## Reading and analyzing data\n    77\t\n    78\t### Quick text dump\n    79\t```bash\n    80\t# Tab-separated rows under `## Sheet:` headers\n    81\textract-text file.xlsx | head -100\n    82\t# .xlsm: same zip structure, override the extension\n    83\textract-text --format xlsx file.xlsm | head -100\n    84\t```\n    85\t\n    86\t### Data analysis with pandas\n    87\tFor data analysis, visualization, and basic operations, use **pandas** which provides powerful data manipulation capabilities:\n    88\t\n    89\t```python\n    90\timport pandas as pd\n    91\t\n    92\t# Read Excel\n    93\tdf = pd.read_excel('file.xlsx')  # Default: first sheet\n    94\tall_sheets = pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', sheet_name=None)  # All sheets as dict\n    95\t\n    96\t# Analyze\n    97\tdf.head()      # Preview data\n    98\tdf.info()      # Column info\n    99\tdf.describe()  # Statistics\n   100\t\n   101\t# Write Excel\n   102\tdf.to_excel('output.xlsx', index=False)\n   103\t```\n   104\t\n   105\t## Excel File Workflows\n   106\t\n   107\t## CRITICAL: Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values\n   108\t\n   109\t**Always use Excel formulas instead of calculating values in Python and hardcoding them.** This ensures the spreadsheet remains dynamic and updateable.\n   110\t\n   111\t### \u274c WRONG - Hardcoding Calculated Values\n   112\t```python\n   113\t# Bad: Calculating in Python and hardcoding result\n   114\ttotal = df['Sales'].sum()\n   115\tsheet['B10'] = total  # Hardcodes 5000\n   116\t\n   117\t# Bad: Computing growth rate in Python\n   118\tgrowth = (df.iloc[-1]['Revenue'] - df.iloc[0]['Revenue']) / df.iloc[0]['Revenue']\n   119\tsheet['C5'] = growth  # Hardcodes 0.15\n   120\t\n   121\t# Bad: Python calculation for average\n   122\tavg = sum(values) / len(values)\n   123\tsheet['D20'] = avg  # Hardcodes 42.5\n   124\t```\n   125\t\n   126\t### \u2705 CORRECT - Using Excel Formulas\n   127\t```python\n   128\t# Good: Let Excel calculate the sum\n   129\tsheet['B10'] = '=SUM(B2:B9)'\n   130\t\n   131\t# Good: Growth rate as Excel formula\n   132\tsheet['C5'] = '=(C4-C2)/C2'\n   133\t\n   134\t# Good: Average using Excel function\n   135\tsheet['D20'] = '=AVERAGE(D2:D19)'\n   136\t```\n   137\t\n   138\tThis applies to ALL calculations - totals, percentages, ratios, differences, etc. The spreadsheet should be able to recalculate when source data changes.\n   139\t\n   140\t## Common Workflow\n   141\t1. **Choose tool**: pandas for data, openpyxl for formulas/formatting\n   142\t2. **Create/Load**: Create new workbook or load existing file\n   143\t3. **Modify**: Add/edit data, formulas, and formatting\n   144\t4. **Save**: Write to file\n   145\t5. **Recalculate formulas (MANDATORY IF USING FORMULAS)**: Use the scripts/recalc.py script\n   146\t   ```bash\n   147\t   python scripts/recalc.py output.xlsx\n   148\t   ```\n   149\t6. **Verify and fix any errors**: \n   150\t   - The script returns JSON with error details\n   151\t   - If `status` is `errors_found`, check `error_summary` for specific error types and locations\n   152\t   - Fix the identified errors and recalculate again\n   153\t   - Common errors to fix:\n   154\t     - `#REF!`: Invalid cell references\n   155\t     - `#DIV/0!`: Division by zero\n   156\t     - `#VALUE!`: Wrong data type in formula\n   157\t     - `#NAME?`: Unrecognized formula name\n   158\t\n   159\t### Creating new Excel files\n   160\t\n   161\t```python\n   162\t# Using openpyxl for formulas and formatting\n   163\tfrom openpyxl import Workbook\n   164\tfrom openpyxl.styles import Font, PatternFill, Alignment\n   165\t\n   166\twb = Workbook()\n   167\tsheet = wb.active\n   168\t\n   169\t# Add data\n   170\tsheet['A1'] = 'Hello'\n   171\tsheet['B1'] = 'World'\n   172\tsheet.append(['Row', 'of', 'data'])\n   173\t\n   174\t# Add formula\n   175\tsheet['B2'] = '=SUM(A1:A10)'\n   176\t\n   177\t# Formatting\n   178\tsheet['A1'].font = Font(bold=True, color='FF0000')\n   179\tsheet['A1'].fill = PatternFill('solid', start_color='FFFF00')\n   180\tsheet['A1'].alignment = Alignment(horizontal='center')\n   181\t\n   182\t# Column width\n   183\tsheet.column_dimensions['A'].width = 20\n   184\t\n   185\twb.save('output.xlsx')\n   186\t```\n   187\t\n   188\t### Editing existing Excel files\n   189\t\n   190\t```python\n   191\t# Using openpyxl to preserve formulas and formatting\n   192\tfrom openpyxl import load_workbook\n   193\t\n   194\t# Load existing file\n   195\twb = load_workbook('existing.xlsx')\n   196\tsheet = wb.active  # or wb['SheetName'] for specific sheet\n   197\t\n   198\t# Working with multiple sheets\n   199\tfor sheet_name in wb.sheetnames:\n   200\t    sheet = wb[sheet_name]\n   201\t    print(f\"Sheet: {sheet_name}\")\n   202\t\n   203\t# Modify cells\n   204\tsheet['A1'] = 'New Value'\n   205\tsheet.insert_rows(2)  # Insert row at position 2\n   206\tsheet.delete_cols(3)  # Delete column 3\n   207\t\n   208\t# Add new sheet\n   209\tnew_sheet = wb.create_sheet('NewSheet')\n   210\tnew_sheet['A1'] = 'Data'\n   211\t\n   212\twb.save('modified.xlsx')\n   213\t```\n   214\t\n   215\t## Recalculating formulas\n   216\t\n   217\tExcel files created or modified by openpyxl contain formulas as strings but not calculated values. Use the provided `scripts/recalc.py` script to recalculate formulas:\n   218\t\n   219\t```bash\n   220\tpython scripts/recalc.py <excel_file> [timeout_seconds]\n   221\t```\n   222\t\n   223\tExample:\n   224\t```bash\n   225\tpython scripts/recalc.py output.xlsx 30\n   226\t```\n   227\t\n   228\tThe script:\n   229\t- Automatically sets up LibreOffice macro on first run\n   230\t- Recalculates all formulas in all sheets\n   231\t- Scans ALL cells for Excel errors (#REF!, #DIV/0!, etc.)\n   232\t- Returns JSON with detailed error locations and counts\n   233\t- Works on both Linux and macOS\n   234\t\n   235\t## Formula Verification Checklist\n   236\t\n   237\tQuick checks to ensure formulas work correctly:\n   238\t\n   239\t### Essential Verification\n   240\t- [ ] **Test 2-3 sample references**: Verify they pull correct values before building full model\n   241\t- [ ] **Column mapping**: Confirm Excel columns match (e.g., column 64 = BL, not BK)\n   242\t- [ ] **Row offset**: Remember Excel rows are 1-indexed (DataFrame row 5 = Excel row 6)\n   243\t\n   244\t### Common Pitfalls\n   245\t- [ ] **NaN handling**: Check for null values with `pd.notna()`\n   246\t- [ ] **Far-right columns**: FY data often in columns 50+ \n   247\t- [ ] **Multiple matches**: Search all occurrences, not just first\n   248\t- [ ] **Division by zero**: Check denominators before using `/` in formulas (#DIV/0!)\n   249\t- [ ] **Wrong references**: Verify all cell references point to intended cells (#REF!)\n   250\t- [ ] **Cross-sheet references**: Use correct format (Sheet1!A1) for linking sheets\n   251\t\n   252\t### Formula Testing Strategy\n   253\t- [ ] **Start small**: Test formulas on 2-3 cells before applying broadly\n   254\t- [ ] **Verify dependencies**: Check all cells referenced in formulas exist\n   255\t- [ ] **Test edge cases**: Include zero, negative, and very large values\n   256\t\n   257\t### Interpreting scripts/recalc.py Output\n   258\tThe script returns JSON with error details:\n   259\t```json\n   260\t{\n   261\t  \"status\": \"success\",           // or \"errors_found\"\n   262\t  \"total_errors\": 0,              // Total error count\n   263\t  \"total_formulas\": 42,           // Number of formulas in file\n   264\t  \"error_summary\": {              // Only present if errors found\n   265\t    \"#REF!\": {\n   266\t      \"count\": 2,\n   267\t      \"locations\": [\"Sheet1!B5\", \"Sheet1!C10\"]\n   268\t    }\n   269\t  }\n   270\t}\n   271\t```\n   272\t\n   273\t## Best Practices\n   274\t\n   275\t### Library Selection\n   276\t- **pandas**: Best for data analysis, bulk operations, and simple data export\n   277\t- **openpyxl**: Best for complex formatting, formulas, and Excel-specific features\n   278\t\n   279\t### Working with openpyxl\n   280\t- Cell indices are 1-based (row=1, column=1 refers to cell A1)\n   281\t- Use `data_only=True` to read calculated values: `load_workbook('file.xlsx', data_only=True)`\n   282\t- **Warning**: If opened with `data_only=True` and saved, formulas are replaced with values and permanently lost\n   283\t- For large files: Use `read_only=True` for reading or `write_only=True` for writing\n   284\t- Formulas are preserved but not evaluated - use scripts/recalc.py to update values\n   285\t\n   286\t### Working with pandas\n   287\t- Specify data types to avoid inference issues: `pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', dtype={'id': str})`\n   288\t- For large files, read specific columns: `pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', usecols=['A', 'C', 'E'])`\n   289\t- Handle dates properly: `pd.read_excel('file.xlsx', parse_dates=['date_column'])`\n   290\t\n   291\t## Code Style Guidelines\n   292\t**IMPORTANT**: When generating Python code for Excel operations:\n   293\t- Write minimal, concise Python code without unnecessary comments\n   294\t- Avoid verbose variable names and redundant operations\n   295\t- Avoid unnecessary print statements\n   296\t\n   297\t**For Excel files themselves**:\n   298\t- Add comments to cells with complex formulas or important assumptions\n   299\t- Document data sources for hardcoded values\n If the shaft wobbles:\n\n| Wobble amount | Result |\n|---|---|\n| &lt;0.2mm | Machine runs smoothly, needles pass cleanly |\n| 0.2-0.5mm | Visible vibration, possible needle jams at high RPM |\n| &gt;0.5mm | Will fail - needles catch on cam edges, yarn breaks |\n\nWith a dial indicator you measure this directly. Without one, you can only tell \"does it look wobbly\" by eye - which catches wobble down to about 0.5mm at best.\n\n## When you'd check runout\n\n- **After bearing install** (before Loctite cures) - verify nothing is misaligned\n- **After Loctite cure** - confirm final alignment\n- **When something feels wrong** later - diagnose vibration issues\n\nSo in total, maybe 2-3 actual measurement sessions across the whole build.\n\n## Honest assessment - is it really necessary?\n\n### Arguments FOR having it\n\n1. **Prevents expensive mistakes.** If bearings are misaligned and you glue them with Loctite without checking, you'd have to destroy the printed blocks to fix it.     "text": "## Honest assessment: the reviewer is 100% right\n\nThis is a real design gap. Let me walk through it carefully because I need to be straight with you.\n\n## What \"axial preload\" actually means and why it matters\n\nA thrust bearing only works when its two races are being pressed together. Without that pressure, the balls inside rattle around freely, and you get:\n\n- **Axial play:** shaft moves up and down 0.1-0.5mm each rotation (click-click-click)\n- **Noise under load:** the balls momentarily lose contact then slam back\n- **Accelerated wear:** impact loading instead of smooth rolling\n- **Cassette height variation:** critical for needle-cam alignment\n\n**Preload = constant axial squeeze on the bearing that keeps races engaged regardless of operating conditions.**\n\n## What V2.2 actually has: NO preload\n\nLooking at the current design honestly:\n\n```\n  [shaft] (can slide freely through bearings)\n    |\n  [top bearing inner race] - nothing holds it to shaft\n    |\n  [shaft continues down through air gap] ~8mm\n    |\n  [bottom radial bearing inner race] - nothing holds it to shaft  \n    |\n  [air gap]\n    |\n  [51101 thrust bearing] - sits loose in pocket, inner race free\n    |\n  [washers + PETG floor]\n```\n\n**The shaft can move up and down freely through ALL three bearings.** The bearings don't grip the shaft axially (that's not what they're for). The only things stopping axial motion are:\n\n1. Gravity pulling shaft down (which eventually seats everything)\n2. Shaft collars clamped above/below the blocks (which I mentioned in the assembly stack but never actually designed into the CAD)\n\n**There is NO spring, NO wave washer, NO belleville, NO explicit preload force.**\n\n## I owe you an acknowledgment\n\nI should have flagged this earlier when we designed V2. The reviewer caught something I glossed over - I assumed the external shaft collars would provide axial positioning, but positioning is not preload. Gravity alone is not preload either - it's a variable force that depends on machine orientation and what's mounted on top.\n\n**This IS a real design gap that needs fixing before printing.**\n\n## Three ways to solve this - let me recommend the best\n\n### Option 1: Wave spring washer (industrial standard)\n\nAdd a wave spring between the radial bearing inner race and the thrust bearing. The spring compresses when assembled and provides constant preload.\n\n**Parts needed:**\n- Smalley wave spring 12mm ID x 24mm OD x ~1mm compressed, ~3mm free\n- Amazon search: \"wave spring 12mm shaft bearing preload\"\n- ~$8-12 for a pack\n\n**Pro:** Professional solution, self-compensating for thermal expansion\n**Con:** Requires macro redesign to accommodate spring height\n\n### Option 2: Belleville (disc spring) washer\n\nSimilar idea but uses a conical spring washer instead of wave shape.\n\n**Parts needed:**\n- Belleville washer 12mm ID x 25mm OD x 1.2mm\n- Amazon search: \"belleville washer 12mm 25mm\"\n- ~$5-8 for a pack\n\n**Pro:** Simpler than wave spring, same effect\n**Con:** Smaller deflection range, less forgiving tolerance\n\n### Option 3: Shaft collar clamping strategy (simplest)\n\nAdd a shaft collar clamped INSIDE the bottom housing block that rests directly on the thrust bearing inner race. When the TOP shaft collar is tightened down hard, it compresses the whole stack from above.\n\n**Parts needed:**\n- Already have! Bottom shaft collar is clamped to shaft at a specific height\n2. When shaft is dropped into the housing, the collar pushes DOWN on the wave spring\n3. Wave spring pushes DOWN on the stack: washers \u2192 thrust bearing \u2192 washers \u2192 PETG floor\n4. The thrust bearing is now PRELOADED with a constant force (spring compression)\n5. Details, verified ASINs for the least-bad Amazon compromises, and the better non-Amazon path below.\n\n## Wave spring: primary and backup recommendations\n\n**The correct part is a single-turn 3-wave disc washer ~0.4\u20130.5 mm thick, not a multi-turn crest-to-crest wave spring.** A true multi-turn Smalley-style spring at your dimensions would have a spring rate of 5\u201315 N/mm because its turns are stacked in series, requiring 2\u20136 mm of deflection to reach 30 N \u2014 far beyond your 1 mm working window. Lisheng's LM-30 catalog, for example, spans 6.7 N/mm (light) to 37.9 N/mm (heavy) only because the heavy variant packs 3.5 waves at 0.46 mm thickness into a single turn. URL: `amazon.com/multi-wave-spring-catalog-17-7PH-compression/dp/B077S9DX92`. Bulk pack will run ~$80\u2013120, blowing past your $5\u201310 budget but giving you a lifetime supply.\n\n**Backup Amazon option \u2014 ASIN B082MYK6G5** (verified). Beveled washers like B0GTN7YRPR \u2014 they tilt the bearing. Second, a **Belleville disc spring will look nearly identical in product photos but has ~10\u00d7 the spring rate of a wave spring**, so a 12\u00d725 Belleville will crush your bearing at 200+ N before you reach 0.5 mm compression. Third, single-turn stamped \"crinkle\" washers typically have only 0.8 mm free height and go solid at 0.5 mm deflection \u2014 you physically cannot get 1 mm of working travel out of them. Fourth, 65Mn carbon steel (standard on cheap Chinese springs) rusts in humid environments; specify 17-7PH or 302 stainless if your shop isn't climate-controlled. assembly step:</strong> The preload collar positioning is what makes this work.\n    Follow exact Z-position specs for the shaft collars.\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f;\">Shaft Collar Positioning (from BOTTOM face of bottom block = Z=0)</h3>\n\n  <table style=\"max-width:800px;\">\n    <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Z Position (mm)</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr><td><strong>Bottom shaft collar</strong></td><td>Z = -2mm</td><td>Just below block, acts as hard stop</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Bottom block bottom face</td><td>Z = 0</td><td>Reference plane</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Bottom block top face</td><td>Z = 35mm</td><td>Bottom housing boundary</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Gap between blocks</td><td>Z = 35 to 40mm</td><td>5mm aluminum plate mount</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Top block bottom face</td><td>Z = 40mm</td><td>Top housing starts</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Top block top face</td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Top housing ends</td></tr>\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar NEUTRAL (touching)</strong></td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Just touches top bearing, no preload</td></tr>\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar WORKING (preloaded)</strong></td><td>Z = 59mm</td><td>1mm compression = ~30N preload</td></tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\">Assembly Sequence (follow in order)</h3>\n\n  <ol style=\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\">\n    <li>Print both bearing housing blocks (V2.3 STL from macro)</li>\n    <li>Clean bearing pockets with IPA, apply Loctite 603 for 51101 thrust bearing</li>\n    <li>Press 51101 thrust bearing onto lower 2x AS1226 washers (in floor pocket)</li>\n    <li>Place upper 2x AS1226 washers above thrust bearing</li>\n    <li>Drop wave spring into spring pocket (sits loosely at free height)</li>\n    <li>Place spacer ring on top of wave spring</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\n    <li><strong>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</strong></li>\n    <li>Mount bottom housing to aluminum plate with M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamp tight)</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom housing, through spring/spacer, through radial bearing</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through top bearing in top housing</li>\n    <li>Slide top shaft collar down until it just touches top bearing (Z=60mm)</li>\n    <li><strong>Push shaft DOWN 1mm firmly, then tighten top collar at Z=59mm</strong></li>\n    <li>Final check: shaft spins freely, NO click, NO axial play</li>\n  </ol>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\">Preload Tuning</h3>\n  <ul style=\"margin-left: 20px;\">\n    <li><strong>Too loose</strong> (hear click or feel play): Loosen top collar, move DOWN 0.2-0.3mm, retighten</li>\n    <li><strong>Too tight</strong> (rotation feels heavy): Loosen top collar, move UP 0.2mm, retighten</li>\n    <li><strong>Correct</strong>: Shaft spins smoothly, zero click, zero axial play</li>\n  </ul>\n\n  <div class=\"alert alert-info\">\n    <strong>Pro tip:</strong> Mark a reference line on the shaft at Z=59mm from bottom face with a marker pen.\n    Makes re-assembly repeatable every time without re-measuring.\n  </div>\n</div>\n\n<!-- <strong>New assembly step:</strong> The preload collar positioning is what makes this work.\\n    Follow exact Z-position specs for the shaft collars.\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f;\\\">Shaft Collar Positioning (from BOTTOM face of bottom block = Z=0)</h3>\\n\\n  <table style=\\\"max-width:800px;\\\">\\n    <thead><tr><th>Component</th><th>Z Position (mm)</th><th>Purpose</th></tr></thead>\\n    <tbody>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Bottom shaft collar</strong></td><td>Z = -2mm</td><td>Just below block, acts as hard stop</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Bottom block bottom face</td><td>Z = 0</td><td>Reference plane</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Bottom block top face</td><td>Z = 35mm</td><td>Bottom housing boundary</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Gap between blocks</td><td>Z = 35 to 40mm</td><td>5mm aluminum plate mount</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Top block bottom face</td><td>Z = 40mm</td><td>Top housing starts</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Top block top face</td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Top housing ends</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar NEUTRAL (touching)</strong></td><td>Z = 60mm</td><td>Just touches top bearing, no preload</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td><strong>Top collar WORKING (preloaded)</strong></td><td>Z = 59mm</td><td>1mm compression = ~30N preload</td></tr>\\n    </tbody>\\n  </table>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\\\">Assembly Sequence (follow in order)</h3>\\n\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\\\">\\n    <li>Print both bearing housing blocks (V2.3 STL from macro)</li>\\n    <li>Clean bearing pockets with IPA, apply Loctite 603 for 51101 thrust bearing</li>\\n    <li>Press 51101 thrust bearing onto lower 2x AS1226 washers (in floor pocket)</li>\\n    <li>Place upper 2x AS1226 washers above thrust bearing</li>\\n    <li>Drop wave spring into spring pocket (sits loosely at free height)</li>\\n    <li>Place spacer ring on top of wave spring</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603, install 6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\\n    <li><strong>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</strong></li>\\n    <li>Mount bottom housing to aluminum plate with M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamp tight)</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom housing, through spring/spacer, through radial bearing</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through top bearing in top housing</li>\\n    <li>Slide top shaft collar down until it just touches top bearing (Z=60mm)</li>\\n    <li><strong>Push shaft DOWN 1mm firmly, then tighten top collar at Z=59mm</strong></li>\\n    <li>Final check: shaft spins freely, NO click, NO axial play</li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#86198f; margin-top:20px;\\\">Preload Tuning</h3>\\n  <ul style=\\\"margin-left: 20px;\\\">\\n    <li><strong>Too loose</strong> (hear click or feel play): Loosen top collar, move DOWN 0.2-0.3mm, retighten</li>\\n    <li><strong>Too tight</strong> (rotation feels heavy): Loosen top collar, move UP 0.2mm, retighten</li>\\n    <li><strong>Correct</strong>: Shaft spins smoothly, zero click, zero axial play</li>\\n  </ul>\\n\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-info\\\">\\n    <strong>Pro tip:</strong> Mark a reference line on the shaft at Z=59mm from bottom face with a marker pen.\\n    Makes re-assembly repeatable every time without re-measuring.\\n  </div>\\n</div>\\n\\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div Assembly is simpler and more repeatable.\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#1e40af;\">Block Gap Verification (CRITICAL)</h3>\n  <div class=\"action-required\">\n    <h3>Block gap MUST be 11mm</h3>\n    <p>The spacer tube length (29.40mm) was calculated based on:</p>\n    <ul style=\"margin: 5px 0 5px 20px;\">\n      <li>6mm aluminum mounting plate</li>\n      <li>5mm assembly clearance (for fasteners and access)</li>\n      <li><strong>Total: 11mm gap between top of bottom block and bottom of top block</strong></li>\n    </ul>\n    <p><strong>If your actual block gap differs from 11mm, recalculate the spacer length:</strong></p>\n    <p style=\"font-family: monospace; background: #fff; padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px;\">\n      Spacer length = (Block gap) + 18.4mm\n    </p>\n    <p>Examples: gap = 10mm \u2192 spacer 28.4mm. gap = 12mm \u2192 spacer 30.4mm.</p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#1e40af;\">Step-by-step Assembly</h3>\n  <ol style=\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\">\n    <li>Print all 3 STLs from V2.4 macro (top block, bottom block, spacer tube)</li>\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603 to bearing pockets, install:\n      <ul>\n        <li>51101 thrust bearing in bottom block lower pocket</li>\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block upper pocket</li>\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\n      </ul>\n    </li>\n    <li>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</li>\n    <li>In bottom block, stack: lower 2x AS1226 washers \u2192 wave spring \u2192 spacer ring (no Loctite on spring/spacer/washers)</li>\n    <li>Mount bottom block to aluminum plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Mount top block to a separate plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\n    <li>Verify 11mm gap between blocks (use spacer tube as gauge - it should JUST barely touch both bearing inner races when unloaded)</li>\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamped tightly)</li>\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom block</li>\n    <li><strong>Slide spacer tube onto shaft</strong> (sits on bottom radial bearing inner race)</li>\n    <li>Lower top block onto shaft (top bearing slides over shaft, contacts top of spacer tube)</li>\n    <li>Bolt top plate to frame (this defines block gap)</li>\n    <li>Install top shaft collar - <strong>LIGHTLY clamp (retention only, no compression force)</strong></li>\n  </ol>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#1e40af;\">Test Protocol (Verify Preload Works)</h3>\n  <ol style=\"margin-left: 20px;\">\n    <li><strong>Rotation test:</strong> Spin shaft by hand. Should feel smooth with slight resistance.</li>\n    <li><strong>Axial play test:</strong> Try to lift/push shaft. Should be ZERO movement.</li>\n    <li><strong>Click test:</strong> Rotate slowly listening for clicks. Should be silent.</li>\n    <li><strong>Drag test:</strong> Spin shaft, time to coastdown. Should rotate freely 5+ seconds.</li>\n    <li><strong>Runout test:</strong> Use dial indicator. <0.2mm TIR at shaft end.</li>\n    <li><strong>Heat test:</strong> Run 30 RPM for 10 minutes. Should remain cool to touch.</li>\n  </ol>\n\n  <h3 style=\"color:#1e40af;\">Fine-Tuning (if any test fails)</h3>\n  <table>\n    <thead><tr><th>Symptom</th><th>Cause</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>\n    <tbody>\n      <tr><td>Click/rattle on rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too LONG (insufficient preload)</td><td>Shorten spacer 0.1-0.2mm OR remove a shim from the wave spring stack</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Heavy drag, stiff rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too SHORT (excessive preload)</td><td>Add 0.1mm shim above the spacer ring</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Heat buildup</td><td>Excessive preload</td><td>Same as above - reduce preload</td></tr>\n      <tr><td>Axial play (~0.1-0.5mm)</td><td>Spacer too long OR spring damaged</td><td>Shorten spacer; inspect spring for plastic deformation</td></tr>\n    </tbody>\n  </table>\n</div>\n\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\n<div class=\"section\">\n  <h2>Section 1 - All 57 Existing Orders (Status Unchanged)</h2>\n  <div class=\"alert alert-success\">\n    <strong>All 57 existing orders remain valid.</strong> V2.4 is purely additive - no existing parts need to be returned or replaced. Assembly is simpler and more repeatable.\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Block Gap Verification (CRITICAL)</h3>\\n  <div class=\\\"action-required\\\">\\n    <h3>Block gap MUST be 11mm</h3>\\n    <p>The spacer tube length (29.40mm) was calculated based on:</p>\\n    <ul style=\\\"margin: 5px 0 5px 20px;\\\">\\n      <li>6mm aluminum mounting plate</li>\\n      <li>5mm assembly clearance (for fasteners and access)</li>\\n      <li><strong>Total: 11mm gap between top of bottom block and bottom of top block</strong></li>\\n    </ul>\\n    <p><strong>If your actual block gap differs from 11mm, recalculate the spacer length:</strong></p>\\n    <p style=\\\"font-family: monospace; background: #fff; padding: 8px; border-radius: 4px;\\\">\\n      Spacer length = (Block gap) + 18.4mm\\n    </p>\\n    <p>Examples: gap = 10mm \\u2192 spacer 28.4mm. gap = 12mm \\u2192 spacer 30.4mm.</p>\\n  </div>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Step-by-step Assembly</h3>\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px; line-height: 1.8;\\\">\\n    <li>Print all 3 STLs from V2.4 macro (top block, bottom block, spacer tube)</li>\\n    <li>Apply Loctite 603 to bearing pockets, install:\\n      <ul>\\n        <li>51101 thrust bearing in bottom block lower pocket</li>\\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in bottom block upper pocket</li>\\n        <li>6001-2RS radial bearing in top block</li>\\n      </ul>\\n    </li>\\n    <li>Cure Loctite 24 hours at room temperature</li>\\n    <li>In bottom block, stack: lower 2x AS1226 washers \\u2192 wave spring \\u2192 spacer ring (no Loctite on spring/spacer/washers)</li>\\n    <li>Mount bottom block to aluminum plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Mount top block to a separate plate using M5 flathead screws</li>\\n    <li>Verify 11mm gap between blocks (use spacer tube as gauge - it should JUST barely touch both bearing inner races when unloaded)</li>\\n    <li>Install bottom shaft collar at Z = -2mm (clamped tightly)</li>\\n    <li>Insert shaft through bottom block</li>\\n    <li><strong>Slide spacer tube onto shaft</strong> (sits on bottom radial bearing inner race)</li>\\n    <li>Lower top block onto shaft (top bearing slides over shaft, contacts top of spacer tube)</li>\\n    <li>Bolt top plate to frame (this defines block gap)</li>\\n    <li>Install top shaft collar - <strong>LIGHTLY clamp (retention only, no compression force)</strong></li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Test Protocol (Verify Preload Works)</h3>\\n  <ol style=\\\"margin-left: 20px;\\\">\\n    <li><strong>Rotation test:</strong> Spin shaft by hand. Should feel smooth with slight resistance.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Axial play test:</strong> Try to lift/push shaft. Should be ZERO movement.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Click test:</strong> Rotate slowly listening for clicks. Should be silent.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Drag test:</strong> Spin shaft, time to coastdown. Should rotate freely 5+ seconds.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Runout test:</strong> Use dial indicator. <0.2mm TIR at shaft end.</li>\\n    <li><strong>Heat test:</strong> Run 30 RPM for 10 minutes. Should remain cool to touch.</li>\\n  </ol>\\n\\n  <h3 style=\\\"color:#1e40af;\\\">Fine-Tuning (if any test fails)</h3>\\n  <table>\\n    <thead><tr><th>Symptom</th><th>Cause</th><th>Fix</th></tr></thead>\\n    <tbody>\\n      <tr><td>Click/rattle on rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too LONG (insufficient preload)</td><td>Shorten spacer 0.1-0.2mm OR remove a shim from the wave spring stack</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Heavy drag, stiff rotation</td><td>Spacer tube too SHORT (excessive preload)</td><td>Add 0.1mm shim above the spacer ring</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Heat buildup</td><td>Excessive preload</td><td>Same as above - reduce preload</td></tr>\\n      <tr><td>Axial play (~0.1-0.5mm)</td><td>Spacer too long OR spring damaged</td><td>Shorten spacer; inspect spring for plastic deformation</td></tr>\\n    </tbody>\\n  </table>\\n</div>\\n\\n<!-- ==================================================================== -->\\n<div class=\\\"section\\\">\\n  <h2>Section 1 - All 57 Existing Orders (Status Unchanged)</h2>\\n  <div class=\\\"alert alert-success\\\">\\n    <strong>All 57 existing orders remain valid.</strong> V2.4 is purely additive - no existing parts need to be returned or replaced. Bottom bearing housing block (80\u00d780\u00d735mm) \u2014 V2.3 stack with 1.4mm spring pocket\n3. **Spacer tube (NEW)** \u2014 12.2mm ID \u00d7 18mm OD \u00d7 29.40mm long\n\n## The math behind 29.40mm\n\n| Component | Dimension |\n|---|---|\n| Bottom radial bearing top face | Z = 27.4mm |\n| Block gap (locked) | 11.0mm (6mm Al plate + 5mm clearance) |\n| Top bearing bottom face | Z = 57.7mm |\n| **Distance between inner races** | **30.3mm** |\n| Spring compression target | 0.5mm (yields ~30N preload) |\n| Tolerance margin | 0.4mm |\n| **Spacer length** | **29.40mm \u00b10.05mm** |\n\nWhen the assembly closes up, the spacer tube cannot reach both bearing inner races. The 0.5mm gap is closed by spring compression \u2014 automatically and repeatably.\n\n## V2.4 changes from V2.3\n\n| Change | From | To |\n|---|---|---|\n| Spacer tube | none | **NEW: 29.40mm rigid tube** |\n| Spring pocket depth | 1.2mm | 1.4mm (assembly safety margin) |\n| Block gap | undefined | **LOCKED at 11mm** |\n| Top collar role | preload setter (Z=59mm) | retention only (light clamp) |\n| Assembly steps | 11 steps with manual compression | 10 steps, no manual tuning |\n\n## New hardware (~$25-30 total)\n\n| Item | Source | Price |\n|---|---|---|\n| Wave spring (V2.3 carryover) | McMaster-Carr | $10 |\n| Spacer ring (V2.3 carryover) | McMaster-Carr | $10 |\n| **Spacer tube (V2.4 NEW)** | Aluminum tube cut to 29.40mm | **$10** |\n\nThe spacer tube has three options:\n- **Option A:** Aluminum tube cut and filed to 29.40mm (~$10) - **recommended for production**\n- **Option B:** PETG print first (free) - **good for prototype testing**\n- **Option C:** Ground steel tube ($15-30) - **elite/lifetime durability**\n\n**Recommended path:** Print PETG first to validate the geometry, then upgrade to aluminum once you confirm the 29.40mm length is correct for your actual block gap.\n\n## Updated project total\n\n| | Amount |\n|---|---|\n| Already spent (57 orders) | $1,263.84 |\n| Mandatory returns | -$58.99 |\n| V2.4 hardware (3 items) | +$30 |\n| Wood base + essentials | +$22 |\n| **PROJECT TOTAL (V2.4 minimum)** | **$1,224.96** |\n| With all optional items | $1,315.96 |\n\n**Still within $1,230-1,500 budget.**\n\n## Critical assembly note\n\n**Block gap MUST be 11mm.** The spacer length was calculated assuming 11mm gap. Yours doesn't have that.\n\n## Three paths forward \u2014 which do you want?\n\n### Path A: Drive hub COUPLES the supplied pulley to the cassette base\n**What it does:** The 60T pulley clamps directly to the shaft via its own set screw. The \"drive hub\" is a printed part that sits **above the pulley**, clamps to the shaft, and has **4 bolts going UP into the cassette base** (not into the pulley).\n\n**Function:**\n```\nCassette base (above)\n   |\n   | <- 4x M5 bolts from drive hub UP into cassette\n   |\n[Drive Hub] (12mm clamp on shaft)\n   |\n   | <- 60T pulley on shaft below, with own set screw\n   |\n[60T HTD 5M pulley]\n```\n\n**Pros:**\n- Uses your existing pulley as-is (no drilling)\n- Drive hub is purely a printed part\n- Standard architecture in industrial CSM machines\n\n**Cons:**\n- More vertical stack height\n- Two clamping points on shaft (pulley + hub)\n\n### Path B: Drive hub REPLACES the pulley's hub interface\n**What it does:** You drill 4 holes through the 60T pulley flange. The printed drive hub bolts to the pulley with M5 screws AND clamps to the shaft. This is what the reviewer's macro builds.\n\n**Function:**\n```\nCassette base (above)\n   |\n   | <- bolts from cassette down to drive hub\n   |\n[Drive Hub] (12mm shaft clamp + 4 holes for pulley)\n   |\n   | <- 4x M5 bolts down to pulley flange\n   |\n[60T HTD 5M pulley] (drilled with 4 M5 holes)\n```\n\n**Pros:**\n- Compact stack (hub and pulley combine into one unit)\n- More rigid coupling (bolts + clamp)\n\n**Cons:**\n- Requires precision drilling 4 holes in the aluminum pulley (need drill press, layout)\n- Risk of damaging pulley if drilling goes wrong\n- Pulley already has hub - drilling weakens it\n\n### Path C: Skip the printed hub entirely\n**What it does:** Use the 60T pulley as-is, mount the cassette directly to the pulley flange (drill 4 holes in the pulley anyway).\n\n**Pros:**\n- Fewer parts\n- Maximum rigidity\n\n**Cons:**\n- Same drilling concern as Path B\n- Cassette bottom needs to mate with pulley flange geometry\n- Less standardized\n\n## My strong recommendation: **Path A**\n\nPath A is the cleanest, lowest-risk approach for a DIY project:\n- No drilling of the aluminum pulley (which can go wrong)\n- Drive hub is purely a printed/replaceable part \u2014 if you mess it up, just reprint\n- Uses your supplied pulley exactly as-is, set screw and all\n- Industrial CSM machines (Lonati style) typically use this architecture\n\nThe slight increase in vertical stack height is irrelevant for our application.\n\n## Question for you\n\n**Which path do you want me to build the macro for?**\n\n- **A** \u2014 Drive hub above 60T pulley, hub bolts to cassette (my recommendation)\n- **B** \u2014 Drive hub clamps shaft AND bolts to drilled pulley flange (reviewer's design)\n- **C** \u2014 Skip printed hub, drill pulley directly for cassette mounting\n\nOnce you pick, I'll need a few more specs:\n\n1. **Cassette base thickness** \u2014 what's the bottom of your cassette? (I have it as 10mm PETG with M5 inserts from project memory)\n2. **Bolts for cassette mount** \u2014 should I use M5 (matching your existing inserts)?\n3. **PCD for cassette bolts** \u2014 typical is 60-80mm. Pick what feels right or I can recommend.\n\nOr just say \"Path A, you decide the rest\" and I'll use sensible defaults that match your existing hardware (M5, 70mm PCD, 4 bolts, fits within cassette base diameter of 150mm).",
